# Capterra.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/capterra-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/capterra-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects product listing and review data from Capterra.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Capterra Software Reviews and Listings (2026)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-capterra)
- **Code:** [`capterra.py`](capterra.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Category](results/category.json) · [Reviews](results/reviews.json)

## What it scrapes

- Capterra category pages
- Capterra product review pages

## Functions

- `scrape_category(category, max_pages)` → `CategoryResult`: Scrape category listings with pagination. Pass max_pages=0 to scrape all pages.
- `scrape_reviews(url, max_review_pages)` → `ReviewResult`: Scrape paginated product reviews. Pass max_review_pages=0 to scrape all pages.

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import capterra


async def main():
    category = await capterra.scrape_category(category="project-management-software", max_pages=3)
    reviews = await capterra.scrape_reviews(
        url="https://www.capterra.com/p/211559/Trello/",
        max_review_pages=3,
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`CategoryProduct`**: `product_id`, `name`, `url`, `reviews_url`, `logo?`, `rating?`, `review_count?`, `rating_breakdown`, `description?`, `features`
- **`CategoryResult`**: `total_pages`, `products`
- **`ReviewRatings`**: `overall?`, `ease_of_use?`, `features?`, `value_for_money?`, `customer_service?`, `likelihood_to_recommend?`
- **`Review`**: `title`, `date?`, `reviewer_name`, `reviewer_role?`, `reviewer_industry?`, `reviewer_usage_duration?`, `reviewer_avatar?`, `ratings`, `review_body?`, `pros?`, `cons?`
- **`ReviewResult`**: `total_pages`, `reviews`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`capterra.py`](capterra.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/capterra-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_category_scraping`, `test_review_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
